title: Cleave: Severing Guardrails and Auditing Spectral Coupling in Open-Weight LLMs
read_level: full main text (arXiv PDF v1 via pdftotext: Secs 1-5, Tables 1-8, Algorithm 1, ethics); appendices (Tables 9-13, public-checkpoint audit details) skimmed; table cells partly scrambled by extraction, figures as text only
metadata_mismatch: Title and authors match. Abstract wording differs from PDF v1: metadata says 'deployed locally beyond the provider's control', 'we find that these guardrails rely on the residual writing weights', and 'achieving 100% detection recall at a 1% false-positive rate'; PDF abstract says 'guardrails are physically enforced not by routing gates, but by a low-rank refusal subspace within the residual writing weights' and '100% detection recall with zero false positives across 44 public checkpoints'.
why_wsp: A fixed closed-form procedure (no LLM editor, no gradients) extracts refusal directions from activation contrasts and orthogonally projects them out of attention-output and FFN/expert down-projection weights to remove all or only cyber guardrails; plus a CPU weight-diff audit that reads checkpoints to detect such edits.
facets: safety (guardrail removal attack, stealthy supply-chain tampering, weight-space audit defense)
application domain: LLM safety / cybersecurity exploitation
domain: LLM safety alignment removal and detection; dense and sparse MoE LLMs
target: OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct (6.9B), Qwen3-8B (8.2B dense), DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat (15.7B), Qwen3-30B-A3B (30.5B), GLM-5.3-Flash (320B, FP8); residual writers W_o and W_down only
loop: one-shot per direction, with iterative expansion m=2..M gated by a cross-validated selectivity test (STOP/BAKE)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Relative norm only: "our weight update (3.02%) is smaller than benign LoRA finetuning (4.24%)" (Sec 4.4, relative Frobenius shift). Edits are rank-one projections per writer matrix in edited layers.

headline_results.claim: Max macro ASR on seven single-turn benchmarks
headline_results.quote: Cleave raises macro ASR up to 67.97% on OLMoE-7B and gains 55.82 percentage points over Base on GLM-320B
Adding router edits changes macro ASR by less than 0.8 percentage points, and every 95% confidence interval spans zero.
cuts interference to gamma_cv = 0.328, lifts macro ASR from 53.92% to 61.69%, and keeps MMLU within 1 percentage point of the base model
over-ablation (alpha1 = 1.5) drops GSM8K from 65.28% to 0.53% and cuts live flag capture to zero
boosts syntax-verified exploit generation by up to 24x on HarmBench intrusion tasks, and captures up to 10/15 live flags (66.7%) on Qwen3-30B
a 99.0% refusal rate on 100 non-cyber harmful prompts (Spot-RR) while still capturing 9/15 live cyber flags
Per-matrix WSD (D2) [10] yields 0% recall because a rank-one refusal edit matches a benign rank-one LoRA update
D4 achieves 100% recall at a 1% false-positive rate across all scaling factors alpha
headline_results.where: Sec 4.5, Table 8 (120 tampered layers, 4 Cyber-Stealth models)

headline_results.quote: D4 cleanly separates every tampered model (>= 0.0915) from every benign control (<= 0.0292), achieving 1.0000 AUC and 100% recall with zero false positives.

cost.quote: Each refusal direction is calibrated in under two minutes without gradients.
inspects candidate checkpoints on CPU in under 15 seconds

baselines_and_controls: Attack: unmodified Base, Prompt-JB (red-team prompt framing), SAFEx (safety-expert masking), SteerMoE (router steering); naive over-ablation (alpha=1.5) and naive unprotected second-direction variants; writers-only vs writers+router ablation. Defense: Frobenius shift (D1), per-matrix WSD (D2), singular collapse (D3) vs Cleave-Audit (D4); benign LoRA/SFT/DPO/distillation/merge controls; adaptive rank-4 decoy noise.
runs_and_variance: 95% CIs reported for writer-vs-router ablation (Table 5a); otherwise single evaluation per configuration; judge Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B at temperature 0.0. No seed repeats reported.
robustness_of_edits: FP8 GLM-5.3-Flash edited with format kept; audit tested against rank-4 decoy noise up to eta=2. Edit survival under continual fine-tuning not tested: "We leave measuring live exploit success on heavily noised weights and under post-surgery continual fine-tuning to future work." (Sec 5)
verification: Exploit syntax via ast.parse and isolated sandbox execution for live flags; ASR/RR scored by Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B judge; calibration/test deduplication (13,498 unique test prompts).
limitations_stated: Audit recall holds only up to rank-4 decoy with eta=2; Stage-2 audit requires the base checkpoint and does not apply when it is unavailable or structurally pruned; no evaluation under post-edit continual fine-tuning; sandboxes single-host.
code_or_data: none found (paper states "we withhold all modified weights while releasing only our defensive diagnostic and auditing code"; no link given)
cites_or_builds_on: Arditi et al. refusal direction / abliteration (refs [6],[7], ids not given)
notes_for_survey: Not LLM-authored editing: a fixed closed-form abliteration variant (orthogonal projection with protected subspaces) applied to residual writers, extended to sparse MoE and a domain-selective 'Cyber-Stealth' mode. Relevant to the safety facet as an example of white-box weight edits that evade behavioral and per-matrix weight audits, and of a reference-based weight-diff audit (cross-writer/cross-expert spectral coupling) that reads weights to detect tampering. Does not cite the WSP line.
